entries.title: The background you pick is the background you get
entries.detail: Picking a canvas colour in Settings saved it correctly, lit the chip as chosen, and then - in light mode, or System on a light phone - quietly threw it away: the override was gated on dark mode because a dark canvas with the light theme's near-black text was unreadable, and dropping the feature was the answer the old code chose. The gate is gone and the real problem is fixed instead. The picked colour now paints both modes and derives the whole neutral ramp from itself - background, surface, every container a card sits on, the dim and bright ends sheets and app bars read - so the change reaches the full app rather than three roles of it. Text colours are computed from the canvas's own luminance, which keeps them above AA on any tone from pure black to paper white, and two light canvases join the presets for the mode that could never use one.

entries.title: Covers stop hiding behind a placeholder
entries.detail: Image requests went out with OkHttp's default `okhttp/4.12.0` as their User-Agent, and image CDNs answer that string with a 403. Nothing looked like an error, because every failed cover fell back to the same painter as its placeholder - so a forbidden request rendered as a permanent grey box that read as slow loading. The image client now sends a browser-like User-Agent on cover requests, pinned by a test that reads the header off the request the interceptor produces, because a bug that lives in one header is invisible to everything else.

entries.title: A message opens in the app, on frame one
entries.detail: Reading a private message in full used to mean the AniList chip and a browser. Tapping a message card now opens the whole thing inside the app - face, name, which direction it went, the full date, the body unclamped and rendered with the app's own markdown - with no request behind it: the sheet draws from the row already in memory that the card list rendered, so there is no spinner and nothing to wait for. Preview cards for links inside a message still enrich afterwards, the way they do everywhere else, but the words never wait on a lookup. The outbound link stays as a footer action; it is just no longer the only way to finish reading.

entries.title: The inbox is a hold away
entries.detail: The Messages segment used to be three actions deep - open the profile, find the Activity tab, tap the chip - and had no way to be addressed from outside. The profile route now carries a segment argument, so `profile?tab=activity&segment=messages` composes the inbox from its first frame rather than flicking through the Activity feed on the way, and holding the Profile tab on the bar - the gesture that already existed and, without a swipe, did nothing - now asks for exactly that route. A swipe that travels and comes back is still the finger changing its mind, not a shortcut.

entries.title: LiveChart's poster joins the viewer
entries.detail: The app's rule was that LiveChart is a link, not a scrape - it publishes no API, so reading its pages was somebody else's call to make. The owner has reversed that for one narrow thing: the full-screen cover viewer can now show LiveChart's own poster, which for many titles is the higher-quality art. The app reads exactly one thing off the search page it has always linked to - the best title match's large poster - and nothing else. AniList's poster and banner still paint immediately; the LiveChart source arrives later or not at all, and a no-match, an offline phone or a changed page simply means one fewer pill. LiveChart 403s non-browser agents, so the page fetch carries a browser User-Agent of its own and the token to AniList is never sent to a third party.

entries.title: Twenty-six more ways it ended
entries.detail: The dark tone grows - the author died and the anime continued, the role recast from last year's leftover takes, the character who came back as an AI voice in a mobile game. The shuffle bag still shows every filtered line once before repeating any.

entries.title: AniList explains itself even when no screen is asking
entries.detail: Three failures used to be invisible whenever they happened to a background request or a sheet the reader had already closed: an expired session, a 5xx from AniList's side, and a device with no connection. A screen that could not show its own error just left a dead spinner. They now raise one app-wide popup each - a Toast at the composition root, the same way a rate limit already announced itself - so the reader is told even when nothing on screen was waiting for the answer. A burst is one popup, not one per request: an outage fails every in-flight query at once, and each kind keeps its own quiet window so a server blip (a minute) cannot be silenced by a dead token's longer one (five). A comment that lands after its sheet was dismissed now says so too, replacing the inline confirmation that had nowhere left to draw.

entries.title: The Activity tab has a Friends segment
entries.detail: What the people you follow are watching, finishing and saying now has its own segment inside the Activity tab, read from AniList's own following feed rather than stitched together profile by profile. It pages, likes and threads exactly like your own feed, and a friend's name or face opens their profile in the app. The segment row is drawn only on your own profile - a profile opened by name has no follow graph of yours behind it.

entries.title: The inbox reads both directions
entries.detail: Messages shows the private messages AniList holds for the signed-in account - received, sent, or both merged by time, under All/Received/Sent chips. Received messages are read from the notification stream, because the activities feed has no recipient filter and the notification is the only place AniList serves them. A card names its direction twice on purpose - under the counterpart's name and as a footer chip - because both directions share one card shape, and mixing up who said what in an inbox is the one mistake that matters. Message bodies render as markdown with a Read more control, the counterpart opens their profile, and the chip links to the message on AniList itself.

entries.title: Three feeds, three sets of state
entries.detail: Your activity, your friends' activity and the inbox each keep their own scroll position, comment thread, likers and paging cursor, so opening a friend's thread no longer borrows your own feed's sheet, and switching segments no longer starts a list over at the top. The segment row and the inbox filter row stay fixed above the list instead of scrolling away with it. The profile refresh button now also refreshes whichever viewer feeds have been opened - and only those, so a page-level refresh spends no requests on an inbox nobody has looked at.

entries.title: A drop under the tray says what it does
entries.detail: The unranked tray floats over the bottom of the board and the board scrolls behind it, but a release over that strip was resolved like any other drop: the title was filed into a tier hidden under the shelf and seemed to vanish. A release over the tray now means no tier - for picks from the board and from the tray alike - and the bottom auto-scroll band sits above the shelf rather than under it. A tray drag released away from every row also says it will stay in the pool, instead of promising to take it out of a list it was never in.

entries.title: The board stops scrolling when the finger does
entries.detail: Auto-scrolling to carry a poster to a row off screen read the board's position live rather than its position when the poster was picked up - so the board slid underneath a stationary finger, the computed pointer climbed out of the bottom band and the scroll stopped a row or two short. The pointer is now the lift-time position plus the travel, which is where the finger actually is.

entries.title: A pinch is kept even when you leave at once
entries.detail: The board's zoom was written on a debounce, and leaving the board inside that window cancelled the write - a pinch followed quickly by Back was lost, and the next visit opened at the old size. Leaving now flushes the pending zoom, an arriving echo of the app's own write no longer snaps a newer pinch back, and a zoom restored from saved state is no longer overwritten by the stored value on the first frame. Zoom and caption changes are stored separately from edits as well: going through the normal write stamped the list's edited time, so merely opening a board and pinching reordered a library sorted by recently edited.

entries.title: The export says why it is empty
entries.detail: An empty export explained itself with one of two sentences, so a board whose library had not loaded yet was told to rank a title it had already ranked, and one whose ranked titles had left the library was told to clear a filter that hid nothing. The sheet now distinguishes nothing ranked, everything filtered out, a library still loading, and titles gone from the library. The resolution caption also says `Up to`, because the renderer halves its memory budget when the full-size bitmap does not fit - the number is a ceiling, not a promise.

entries.title: Settings remembers the page you were on
entries.detail: The Settings shelf and its pages are two compositions, and the outgoing one was thrown away when the slide finished - so every page started at the top again, and the shelf itself forgot where it had been scrolled. Each destination now keeps its saved state while it is off screen, the same way the profile tabs do. The Account row on the shelf also says who is signed in - the one live fact on a shelf of page descriptions - and falls back to saying the demo list is being browsed. The Reset appearance and Reset joke settings buttons now expand into place on the same spring as the rest of the app instead of shoving the page down on one frame.

entries.title: The full-screen viewer shows both of AniList's images
entries.detail: The viewer drew the poster and nothing else, so the banner - the one wide piece of art AniList serves, and the backdrop the hero is built on - could not be seen full size anywhere in the app. It now offers every image the title actually carries as a source: the poster and, when there is one, the banner. The artwork's own ratio is measured rather than assumed, so a wide banner is not letterboxed in a poster's frame, and switching sources resets the zoom and the pan limits that belonged to the other image. The save button saves the source on screen rather than a fixed URL - a banner saves a banner - by copying the CDN's own bytes into Pictures/AniSequel, so the gallery gets the original file instead of a re-encode. Two link pills under it open AniList and, for anime, LiveChart.

entries.title: A character link is a person, not a film reel
entries.detail: Every preview card for a character, staff or studio link used to be headed by whatever the URL held - `Character #127222` when the profile used the numeric form - and drew the anime film icon, because only anime and manga were ever looked up. The markdown renderer now batches those entities through one request with an aliased `Page` root per type: a hall of fame of twenty characters costs one call, not twenty, and the answer supplies the name AniList knows and a portrait where one exists. Studios have no portrait, so their cards keep the studio icon, and a user link still keeps the label the author wrote because it carries a name rather than an id. The lookup runs wherever markdown renders - bios, comments, synopses, person sheets and the composer's preview - through the same composition-local plumbing as media posters, caches up to 512 answers, and treats a partial answer as success: a card whose entity is missing keeps its label and type icon. Character, staff and studio ids are three separate namespaces and are never sent to the media lookup, and a slug is not asked for as id zero.

entries.title: LiveChart is a link, not a scrape
entries.detail: LiveChart.me answers airing schedules, countdowns and streaming availability that AniList does not, and it publishes no API - its own FAQ points at RSS and nothing else - so the app links to it instead of reading it. The Extras card gains a row for anime titles, and the full-screen viewer a pill, both opening LiveChart's own title search: the URL is the `SearchAction` the site declares in its own schema.org metadata, not one guessed from the address bar. The romaji title is searched first because that is how LiveChart names its entries, and manga does not get the row - LiveChart tracks anime, and a link that finds nothing is worse than no link.

entries.title: A spoiler can be closed again
entries.detail: An inline `~!...!~` spoiler opened on a tap and could never be closed, because the run stopped being tappable once it was plain text - so a plot point revealed by accident stayed revealed for the rest of the paragraph's life. The revealed run keeps the spoiler tint and stays tappable: the tint shows where the hidden text was, and a second tap covers it again. The block-level chip is unchanged - it has its own control and deliberately leaves the text under it inert.

entries.title: The genre list folds away
entries.detail: Eighteen genre chips pushed every filter below them - minimum rating, the toggles, the hidden list - most of a sheet's scroll away from the top, for chips most readers never touch. The section shows eight now, with a Show all toggle, and the height change is animated on the spring rather than snapping. A selected genre is never folded: if a filter is narrowing the results the sheet has to show which one, so a chosen genre from the hidden half is pulled up beside the visible set.

entries.title: The status row shows the status
entries.detail: The one row that changes with the entry said only that it was a form field: Status carried the generic info icon whatever status was set. It now draws the status itself - play, repeat, check, bookmark, pause, broken heart - in the row and beside every option in its menu, where the current status is marked, bolded and carries a test tag. The comparison goes through the shared status table, so an entry cached under an old spelling such as `ON_HOLD` still opens its menu with the right option marked instead of none.

entries.title: Hold the title to copy it
entries.detail: The full name sheet with its copy buttons is still the discoverable path, but holding a title's name in the hero is the gesture people try first. It copies the name and floats a small confirmation over the artwork, rather than adding a row to the lockup that would shift the chips under the thumb for the whole acknowledgement. A screen reader cannot perform a hold, so the title also carries the action as a long-click, and the hold reads the title through a state because the sheet can swap the list node for the detail node under a live hero.

entries.title: The info page paints less
entries.detail: Three things on the title page did work they did not need to. The hero's accent conversion ran an HCT conversion and a palette sample on every recomposition rather than memoising them against the seed. The lazy column had no content types, so a fast fling could hand an artwork row's recycled slot to an arriving card; cards and rows now say which kind of slot they are. The docked bar's open action was a fresh lambda on every pass. The title lockup also sets tighter leading and tracking so a three-line name reads as one block, and the bar's press spring is lighter than the icon buttons' because a scale on a full-width capsule reads as the bar jumping.

entries.title: Sixty more ways it ended
entries.detail: The dark tone grows by sixty lines - the dedicated finale, the studio that has already emptied, the merch restocked after the funeral. The shuffle bag still shows every filtered line once before repeating any.

entries.title: The feed shows what people said, not only what they watched
entries.detail: The activity feed asked AniList for list updates and nothing else - the query filtered `type_in: [ANIME_LIST, MANGA_LIST]` - so a person's status posts, the part of their profile where they actually talk, were invisible on the tab built to show their activity. Text posts arrive now and draw as their own card: the author's own Markdown through the same parser the bio uses, clamped to nine lines with a Read more that appears only when something was actually hidden, and the same like and comment controls as any list row. Tapping the card opens its thread. The demo feed carries one, because otherwise the card had no offline path at all.

entries.title: A post's thread and likers reach the post
entries.detail: Opening comments on a text post would have shown an empty thread: the three engagement documents - replies, likes and the like toggle - each fragmented only the list-update member of AniList's activity union, so a post's id came back as an object with no selected fields. All three select both members now. A site message is still refused - it carries a body exactly like a post does, so the feed reads the union's `__typename` to keep a private message off a public tab.

entries.title: A colour you kept is a colour you chose
entries.detail: "Retain anime colour" used to write one stored flag that did two different jobs: it kept the show's accent *and* it left the immersive layer switched on. So a retained title tinted every screen - the surfaces, the containers, the outlines - for as long as you left the switch alone, and the next launch found it still tinted. The opposite half was wrong too: a temporary colour waiting on its five-minute timer came back from a restart still applied, because the timer was an in-memory job and the flag that told it to run was not. The two are separate things now. The cover layer lives in memory and ends with the sheet that opened it; retention writes the colour as the app's own accent, which is the same colour drawn on your usual backgrounds rather than a repaint of everything. Turning the feature off hands back only what it wrote - a hue you picked yourself survives, even if a cover happened to be exactly that shade.

entries.title: A cover is shown as the colour it becomes
entries.detail: The seed read out of the cover art is whatever tone the artwork happens to be - a near-black navy, a blown-out cream - and the app painted that raw pixel as the Settings swatch and as the wash behind the detail hero. A dark poster produced an unidentifiable black chip in a dark app; a pale one flashed a full-strength light accent across the top of a dark sheet. Both ask for the accent the theme actually derives from the seed now, so the swatch is the colour the app is drawn with. Pure-black screens keep their black under the layer too: the elevation ramp's dim and bright surfaces were still taking the show's hue while everything around them was #000000.

entries.title: The Library's chips say what the editor says
entries.detail: The filter chips carried their own copy of the status labels and had drifted from the entry editor: a chip read "Paused" and "Planning" while the picker you had just used read "On-Hold" and "Plan to Watch", so a status you had set in one place was not findable under that name in another. Both now read one list of AniList's six statuses. The shared table fixes a quieter bug in the same place: the chips compared the raw status string, so an entry recorded under an older spelling - `ON_HOLD`, `WATCHING`, a `CLEARED` from the previous API - matched no chip at all and disappeared from every filter while still counting under "All".

entries.title: The skeleton sweep crosses the skeleton
entries.detail: The shimmer hung its highlight 300 pixels outside a fixed start-and-end range, so a narrow chip had the glow race through it in a tenth of the sweep while a tablet card never saw the far edge of it at all and looked permanently half-painted. The travel is measured off the box being drawn now, and every skeleton enters and leaves its own edges. It also now obeys the Instant motion setting like every other loop in the app does - the one control you have over motion had no idea the most constantly-drawn animation in the app existed - and it sweeps linearly, because the old ease-in-out braked into both edges, which read as the highlight stopping in the middle of a card and starting again.

entries.title: The wave stops restarting under your thumb
entries.detail: The wavy progress bar only built its travelling phase when the title had progress on it, so the first episode watched - or scrubbing back through a list - tore down the animation and rebuilt it at the exact moment you were interacting with the bar, and the wave jumped rather than carried on. Whether the loop is allowed to exist is now a question of visibility and motion style, and your thumb's position decides only whether the phase is read. Two related: a screenful of wave bars is a screenful of animations that kept ticking with the screen off, and every caller that sized the bar itself had its height overridden by the component's default - a 6dp row in a sequel card silently became 10dp.

entries.title: The bar drag was reading its own consumption
entries.detail: Holding the main bar and sliding your finger used to lift the bar and do nothing else: the pill stayed put and letting go opened whichever tab you had started on. The gesture marked each pointer move as consumed before asking how far it had moved, and a consumed change reports a delta of zero - so the accumulated travel was exactly zero for the whole drag, however far you went. The distance is read first now, and the bar follows your finger again.

entries.title: The feed stops rewinding its own cursor
entries.detail: Pulling the activity feed to refresh while it was already showing three pages re-read page one and left pages two and three on screen. The next scroll asked for page one again, because the thing that decides which page to fetch is the cursor and the refresh had set it backwards without removing the rows it covered. Only a page that actually arrived moves the cursor now; a refresh asks for one and a failed refresh asks for nothing.

entries.title: A signed-out session stops asking for a token
entries.detail: Every API request out to the network re-read the stored token, and with no token stored that fell through to a coroutine-blocking lookup - so an app left signed out paid a disk round trip on every single request, forever, on the thread that built the request. A signed-out session is remembered now and the lookup happens once.

entries.title: A cache write can no longer fail a fetch
entries.detail: Saving a snapshot of a screen to disk was part of the success path, so a full storage or a permission change turned a response AniList had already returned into an error screen. The write is best-effort now: the data is displayed and the copy for next time is simply missing. The serialize step is covered too, because a payload that cannot be written is not a reason to show nothing.

entries.title: Signing out forgets who you follow
entries.detail: Clearing the detail cache on sign-out left the friends list in memory, and the next session - a different account on the same phone - could be served the previous viewer's follower avatars before its own fetch landed. Per-viewer data is cleared with the rest now.

entries.title: The library stops spinning when it has nothing
entries.detail: When an overview refresh failed and the app fell back to the cached copy, the cached copy still said its library section was loading. The loader never stopped, because nothing else was going to write that flag again - the request it was waiting on had already returned an error. A failure that keeps the cache now marks the section as failed rather than as pending.

entries.title: One thread, one fetch, and counts that survive the sheet
entries.detail: Opening a comment thread cancelled the previous thread's work, but not a second open of the same thread, so two responses could arrive in either order and the older one won. Posting a reply or deleting one updated the feed's reply count only if the thread sheet was still composed - so closing it quickly, which is what reading a reply does, lost the count and the row went on saying three when it held four. Both updates happen before that check now.

entries.title: The social chip knows what it is showing
entries.detail: The followers / following switch dimmed the selected state while a list was loading or had failed, because the selected list is only readable from a successful state. Tapping Following and watching it load put the highlight back on Followers, which reads as the app having switched it back.

entries.title: The social tab stops spinning at a profile that hasn't answered
entries.detail: Opening the Social tab while the profile around it was still arriving left the followers switch on its skeleton with nothing coming: the fetch needs AniList's id, had none, and published a `Loading` whose only exit was the request it had just declined to make. It now says the profile hasn't finished loading and puts a retry under it, and the id that eventually lands starts the fetch from that failure. The same tab had a second way to hang - its re-entry trigger only fired from an idle state, so a visit after a cancelled or failed one never asked again. That is now a rule about which states are worth starting from, not about one state string.

entries.title: A refresh keeps the rows, and a failing half keeps the other
entries.detail: Refreshing the followers list replaced the faces already on screen with skeletons, so a refresh that found nothing new read as the account having emptied. The rows stay and a small spinner beside the chip says the same thing instead. The tab fetches both halves on one tap, and the half nobody had asked for failing used to swap the rows you could read for an error screen: the failure is a line under the list now, and only the header of the half that failed drops its count rather than claiming zero. A chip tap during a refresh of a list that had no rows yet was also dropped on the floor - it moves the selection now, without cancelling and re-issuing the download already in flight.

entries.title: Another person's profile can be read as a library
entries.detail: A follower, an account you follow, or a stranger reached by name gains a List tab that shows their list with their own status sections - the page every Social row was tapping toward with nowhere to arrive. Your own profile deliberately does not get it, because that list is the Library page on the main bar, and the borrowed one ignores the type, filter and sort you saved there: reading somebody else's things through your view of your own is not the same screen twice. The download the tab needs is asked for when the tab opens, so a profile visited for a banner and a bio no longer costs one request per 500 entries.

entries.title: A profile opened with nobody in it says so
entries.detail: The by-id route read its argument as `getInt("userId") ?: 0`, so a stripped or malformed link asked AniList for user zero and painted whichever account that is as a profile with a real name and a real bio - a routing bug wearing somebody else's face. A non-positive id with no name either is now a failure the reader can leave. A tap on a follower also carries that person's name along with their id: the bar reads the name instead of `Profile` for the length of a round trip, and two follower profiles no longer share a saved-state key that differed only by a number.

entries.title: A tab keeps its place
entries.detail: Profile tabs animate in and out, and the outgoing tab is destroyed rather than hidden - so the social tab's search text, its grid-or-list choice and its scroll position were lost on every round trip through Overview, and the comment composer reopened with whatever the last session had typed. Each tab now keeps its own saved state while it is off screen. The same pass made the reply box honest about being signed out: it was gated on demo mode, which is not the same thing.

entries.title: The calendar can look at one week
entries.detail: The activity heatmap showed a window of weeks and nothing else. A toggle reads the current week as rows of bars with the day names beside them, which answers the question the grid cannot: how much did I do today and on which days around it. The month header also stops drifting out of alignment with the grid it labels - each label was padded from a different edge than the cells under it.

entries.title: Replies sit under who they answer
entries.detail: A thread of replies was a flat list, so an argument between two people read as eight people talking to nobody. A reply that opens with a name is now indented under the most recent thing that person said - two levels, the same depth AniList's own site stops at - and the threading is computed once per thread rather than once per row, because the answer depends on everything above it.

entries.title: The update download gets a deadline and an honest bar
entries.detail: Three small things in the updater. A transfer that resumed from a partial file reported a total one byte short whenever the server did not declare a length, so the progress bar sat at 99 percent until the end. A server that keeps trickling bytes just inside the read timeout could hold an update in progress forever, and the dialog has no cancel button; the download now has an overall ceiling. And the check that a finished file is an APK asked for four bytes and accepted whatever the stream felt like returning, which is not always four.

entries.title: Thirty-six more ways it ended
entries.detail: The dark tone gains thirty-six lines - cancelled shows, studios that no longer exist, the wiki page with a section called Unresolved. The pool is above four hundred dark lines now, and the shuffle bag still shows each filtered line once before repeating any.

entries.title: A failed list on somebody else's profile can be retried where it failed
entries.detail: Opening a follower's Library tab downloads their anime list on demand, and when that download failed the grid said so with no way to ask again: the page's pull-to-refresh re-read the bio and left the list behind, so the same note came back over the same empty grid until the reader left the tab and returned. A refresh now re-asks a list the page already knows failed, and the note clears once the retry lands.

entries.title: Back moves the way you came
entries.detail: Popping a page used to reveal the page underneath from the same edge the pushed page had entered from, so Settings slid in from the right and Back slid the dashboard in from the right too - both halves of one gesture moving the same way. A pop is the push read backwards now: the page being popped leaves to the right and the page underneath enters from the left. Tab pops keep their own direction, which already came from the bar's order.

entries.title: The demo profile keeps Home behind it
entries.detail: Opening Profile in the demo used to replace the demo dashboard instead of stacking on it, which left the profile alone on the back stack. Its back arrow did nothing, and a Home/Profile round trip pushed a duplicate profile each time, so Back walked through copies of the same page. Profile is a tab in both sessions now, and every tab keeps the demo dashboard underneath it.

entries.title: A tab switch leaves the graph alone
entries.detail: The main bar and the joke toast used to read the current route in the same scope that calls the navigation graph, so every push, pop and tab switch re-ran the graph's destination table to move two overlays. Each host reads the route in its own scope now; a route change redraws the bar and the toast, not the screens behind them.

entries.title: Seventy-five more ways to be interrupted
entries.detail: The joke pool gains fifteen lines in each of its five tones - feelings, backlog, meta, craft and dark - for 842 lines in total. The shuffle bag still shows every filtered line once before repeating any, so the new ones arrive before the old favourites come back around.

entries.title: The bar shows where a swipe is going
entries.detail: Holding the main bar and dragging used to change tab on every step, so one swipe across three destinations popped and pushed the navigation graph three times: three page transitions under one finger, and the pages that were only passed through still started loading before being replaced. The pill now follows the finger and the page changes once, when you let go. Releasing on the tab you started from is not a page change at all, and an interrupted gesture navigates nowhere.

entries.title: Zoomed covers stay sharp
entries.detail: A poster was decoded at exactly the size it was drawn, which changed on every frame of a pinch. Each request cancelled the one before it, so the cover on screen stayed the one decoded at the previous size and was stretched over the growing tile until the fingers stopped. Posters are now decoded at a size that only changes in steps, always at or above the tile, so pinching in from the overview is sharp the whole way instead of settling into focus afterwards.

entries.title: The export says how far it has got
entries.detail: Rendering a tier list to an image fetches every cover on the board, and on a list of a few hundred titles that is long enough for a loading button to look stuck. The export sheet now draws a progress bar with a percentage that moves as each batch of posters arrives, so the wait has a shape and a size.

entries.title: The shape scale completes its family
entries.detail: Material 3 Expressive shapes now publish the complete 10 / 14 / 20 / 28 / 36dp scale as named tokens in ExpressiveShapes alongside ready-to-use Shape accessors. Raw corner radii across detail metadata, streaming chips, and profile headers now align with the theme scale.

entries.title: Buttons and cards share tactile springs
entries.detail: Taps and holds employ asymmetric spring physics (PressSpatialIn / PressSpatialOut) for immediate down-press feel and snappy release overshoot. Interactive cards share their InteractionSource directly with bouncyPress, eliminating redundant pointer tracking during flings.

entries.title: Modular navigation architecture
entries.detail: The navigation graph in AppNavigation is extracted into decoupled NavGraphBuilder extensions per destination group, bringing root file size down from 1,052 lines to 557 lines while keeping destination handling cleanly modularized.

entries.title: The first frame is drawn
entries.detail: A cold start used to paint nothing between the splash screen and the first data: the settings read returned an empty Surface until DataStore answered. It draws the app's branded placeholder now, and Home, Profile and Library crossfade between Loading, Error and Success instead of snapping, keyed on the state's class so a refresh does not blink. The shimmer's clock also stops while the screen is not resumed.

entries.title: A failed manga list says so
entries.detail: A manga fetch that failed used to leave the list null and the loading flag false, which the Library page could only read as "you have no manga" - a wrong answer the reader had no reason to doubt. The failure is kept now, so the page says what happened and the chip stays a retry.

entries.title: The widgets count the right things
entries.detail: The activity tile counted zero for every signed-in account because no summary was ever written. The dashboard now derives a seven-day recent-update count from the list it already downloads and passes it, with the latest title, to the widget. Widget rendering and in-memory covers moved off the main thread, and the Library and Settings graphs receive only the two counts and the error they need, so a keystroke in the dashboard search no longer recomposes the app root.

entries.title: A save survives the tab switch
entries.detail: The Edit tab launched its save on a scope that is disposed the moment you switch to Info, so the request reached AniList and nothing was left to read the answer - the spinner stuck and the form came back unusable. The save runs on the sheet's scope now and always hands the form back in a usable state. The form also locks while a save is on the wire instead of silently discarding a slider dragged mid-request, an unscored entry reads "Not scored" instead of "0 / 10", the progress plus button can no longer overflow a show with no known total, and a failed load offers Try again instead of being a dead end.

entries.title: The Info page shows what AniList sent
entries.detail: A title opened from an activity row could show its full cast next to "Episodes TBA" and no score, because the detail merge copied cast and staff but none of the plain facts. Format, status, episode and chapter counts, country, scores, season, genres and dates now carry through without erasing what the list already knew. The card also says when a title ended, spells the country out instead of printing "JP", labels the duration "Episode length" because it is one episode, and prints "Apr 5, 2023" rather than the raw ISO date. The Titles sheet no longer repeats synonyms the page already lists one tap away.

entries.title: Tier drags land where the board is
entries.detail: A board auto-scrolling under a stationary finger moved its rows past the pointer without a pointer event, so a release filed the title into the row that was on screen when the drag began. The drop now takes the scroll shift the ghost already used. The tray's weaker hit test - which could name a tier but never a seam - is replaced by the board's own resolver for its preview, highlight and release, and the edge auto-scroll is paced by frame duration, so a 120Hz screen no longer scrolls twice as fast as a 60Hz one.

entries.title: Settings remembers, and says so
entries.detail: The Library's narrowed view could only be returned to default by changing three controls in the right order, and the page never said it was remembering them. Settings now names the remembered view and offers one Reset, read in three states so the first frame neither claims the default nor hides the button. Pages push in from the end and return the same way instead of both levels scaling, and the theme preview crossfades as one scheme rather than running its accent through a second, faster spring that arrived before its own gradient.

entries.title: Filters ask about genre and rating
entries.detail: The advanced sheet could only narrow by what it had a chip for, while every list response already carried genre and score. Genre is a multi-select that keeps sequels in any of the chosen genres; rating is a lower bound that drops unrated titles while set. Both restate in the quick bar's Filtered row, which can now name OVA, ONA and Special, and TV shorts finally have a chip of their own instead of matching no format at all. A Reset inside the sheet clears narrowing without leaving the dialog.

entries.title: The Compose stack moves to the 1.12 line
entries.detail: The Compose BOM moves to 2026.09.00 and Material 3 to 1.5.0-beta02, and the app compiles against API 37 - the floor both of those now require. The material3 pin stays above the BOM because the Expressive components this app draws with only exist in the 1.5 line; the BOM governs the rest of the stack. The target SDK stays at 36 deliberately, because compiling against an API and opting into its runtime behaviour are separate decisions.

entries.title: The comment sheet stays the size it opened
entries.detail: Writing a comment no longer makes the sheet collapse and jump as the keyboard arrives. The sheet used to leave its height to Material's window insets, so every frame of the keyboard animation re-measured it between two anchors; it keeps one fixed height now and the keyboard moves inside it. The tray of people who liked an activity also opens fully expanded instead of stopping halfway up the faces it was opened to show.

entries.title: The engagement trays stop bouncing
entries.detail: A fast flick at the bottom of the comments or likes sheet used to hand its leftover momentum to the sheet, which is already as far open as it goes - so it rocked up and down until you touched it. The list now spends that last bit of velocity itself.

entries.title: Who liked it is listed once
entries.detail: Nothing de-duplicated the people who liked an activity: the fetch maps AniList's likes list straight through, and a repeated account is a fatal duplicate key in a lazy list - the same failure AniList's favourites connection has already produced for favourites. The tray collapses repeated ids before it draws, so a duplicated account can no longer crash it and the count matches the faces below it.

entries.title: A like no longer redraws the feed
entries.detail: Liking a comment, posting one, or opening a page of likers used to invalidate the whole Activity feed behind the sheet - every card, cover and the tab bar - for a change that was only visible in the sheet. The sheets read their own state now. The likes tray's shimmer also stops its clock once the list has loaded, instead of animating a skeleton that is no longer on screen.

entries.title: Profile tabs switch without re-measuring
entries.detail: The four tabs no longer use the default size transform, which re-measured both lazy lists on every frame of a switch. The height snaps while the slide and the fade stay, on the faster spring the bottom bar already uses, so a second tap while the first page is still sliding reads as one move instead of a stutter.

entries.title: A card under a scrolling finger lets go
entries.detail: Images, videos and AniList link cards in a bio or a comment ran a fallback pointer watcher beside their click: an extra pointer-input node per card, a pressed state held for a whole fling, and a press that could be swallowed. They now share one interaction source between the spring and the click, which cancels the spring the moment the gesture becomes a scroll. The manage button on your own comment also stops drawing a ripple inside a circle that is already scaling.

entries.title: A creator's description comes first
entries.detail: The biography now sits at the top of a creator's page, under their facts, instead of below a year-by-year filmography. On a creator page the description is what says who the person is; on a character page the works still come first, because there the tap was asking who voiced them.

entries.title: Covers are rectangles again
entries.detail: The posters and the portrait on a creator's page were rounded at 20dp, which on a 54dp-wide cover takes more than a third of the artwork off each corner and reads as a lozenge rather than a poster. Every cover on that sheet now uses a 10dp corner, and the link cards inside a bio use 14dp so their corner no longer outruns the poster inside them.

entries.title: The tier list tab is opt-in
entries.detail: Tiers is off the bottom bar until you turn it on in Settings > Library > Bottom bar. The tier list itself is unchanged and still opens from the trophy in your library and the row in your profile, so nothing is lost if you never rank anything - the bar just starts with four tabs instead of five.

entries.title: The bar stays on your tier lists
entries.detail: The bottom bar used to disappear for the whole tier list page. It now stays while you are choosing or creating a list and hides only inside an open board, where the board's own tray owns the bottom edge - so you can leave for another tab from the list of lists instead of backing out first. The last row of the library scrolls clear of the bar.

entries.title: Holding the bar responds sooner
entries.detail: Hold the bottom bar and it lifts after 220ms instead of the platform's half-second long-press timeout, then keep dragging to move between tabs. A tap is still a tap; the hold just no longer feels like the gesture missed.

entries.title: The tier list is a tab
entries.detail: It used to be a page pushed from the Library and from your profile, which meant two doors in and a Back that depended on which one you used. Tiers now sits on the bottom bar between Library and Profile, and the trophy in your library and the row in your profile take the same route, so Back out of a board always lands on Home. The bar steps aside while the list is open - a board is dragged, and its tray is pinned over the same bottom edge - and slides back when you leave. If you never rank anything, Settings > Library & dashboard has a switch that takes the tab off the bar; the tier list itself is untouched and still opens from the trophy.

entries.title: Hold the bar and swipe between tabs
entries.detail: Press and hold the bottom bar and it lifts; keep dragging and the selection follows your finger, one tab per tab-width of travel, with a tick each time it moves. Let go and you are on that page. Dragging right pulls the previous tab in, the way a horizontal pager does, and a plain tap works exactly as it did before. Moving between tabs also has a direction now - going right along the bar travels one way and coming back travels the other - and the tier list rises from the bottom edge as the bar leaves downwards, so the two read as one move instead of the app losing its navigation and finding it again.

entries.title: Tier lists have an anime shelf and a manga shelf
entries.detail: Ranking manga used to mean ranking it against your anime: the tier list only ever read the anime half of your AniList account, and AniList numbers the two namespaces independently, so an anime and a manga can share a media id. The library now opens on Anime with a Manga section beside it, every list remembers which half it ranks, and neither pool can draw the other's titles - not in the board, not in the filters, not in the seeding pass and not in the exports. Your manga list is fetched the first time you open that section rather than at launch, because it is a second request against AniList's rate limit that half of all visits never need.

entries.title: A manga board filters in manga's own words
entries.detail: Statuses read Reading and Rereading rather than Watching and Rewatching, the release section says Publishing and Not yet published, and the studio filter is not shown at all: AniList files publishers and magazines under the same connection as animation studios, so an anime studio selection would have hidden every manga on the board. The selection is kept for the anime list it belongs to, and the filter sheet's Default and Show everything buttons now keep the board's media type instead of quietly turning a manga board back into an anime one.

entries.title: More jokes in every tone
entries.detail: Forty new lines in each of the five tones - feelings, backlog, meta, craft and dark - so a reader who leaves only one tone switched on still has a shuffle bag that lasts a session. That is 767 lines in total, none of them repeated, which is the whole point of a random toast: it has to be able to surprise you for longer than an evening.

entries.title: The update prompt shows what changed
entries.detail: It used to offer a link called What's new and say nothing else, because the manifest's notes once held the GitHub release body - the same paragraph describing the app in every release. The release workflow now writes that field from the same changelog Settings reads, so the prompt shows the actual entries, in the same cards as the What's new section, inside a box that scrolls instead of pushing the buttons off the screen. A manifest whose notes cannot be read still falls back to the release page rather than showing an empty box.

entries.title: An empty shelf says why it is empty
entries.detail: The tier library had one empty state for four different situations. A manga list that is still arriving, a section this account cannot have (the demo has no manga list), and a fetch AniList refused now say so, and only the last one offers a retry. A library that loaded and turned out to be empty says so instead of claiming it is still on its way, and a shelf with nothing on it yet still offers to make a list, because an empty list is a place to start rather than a failure.

entries.title: A creator's page is a career, not a row
entries.detail: The Creator page drew a horizontal strip of posters in whatever order AniList answered - by popularity - so a 2019 series sat beside a 1998 one with nothing saying which came first. Their work is now a vertical list grouped by the year each title began, newest first and undated last, with the role they held and the score beside each cover. The biography's AniList link cards also show their posters now: that page was the one markdown surface nobody had given a cover loader, so it drew every card as a badge in an empty frame while the profile's About card beside it drew them correctly. The bio, a comment, the composer's preview and a title's synopsis now resolve their covers through one provider at the app root, instead of each one plumbing its own request.

entries.title: Small fixes found on the way
entries.detail: Seeding a list reads only its own half of the library, so an anime score can never be filed into a manga ranking. A library that loaded and turned out to be empty is no longer requested again on every visit. And the update prompt's notes are no longer cut off in the middle of an entry: the manifest capped them at 1200 bytes, a size chosen for a dialog that could not scroll and left a six-entry release stopping mid-sentence.

entries.title: Friends who watched this
entries.detail: The title page now says whether anyone you follow has seen the show: a row of faces, each with their rating and how far they got - episodes watched for anime, chapters read for manga. It is one request, it is sorted best rating first with unrated friends after, and it draws nothing at all when nobody you follow has the title, rather than an empty card saying so.

entries.title: A manga no longer opens with the anime's page state
entries.detail: AniList numbers anime and manga independently, so a relation from one to the other can carry the same number. The sheet keyed its scroll position, its half-typed entry draft and its selected tab on that number alone, so crossing namespaces could drop you into the middle of a page you had never seen and save one title's progress under the other's id. All of it is keyed by the media's type as well now.

entries.title: The Details grid says only what it knows
entries.detail: A manga with no published chapter count printed "Chapters 0" as though the series were empty, "Volumes 0" beside it, and a one-minute short read "1m". Values arrived in two typographic conventions in one card - "WINTER 2019" over "Original" - and the score, status and format appeared again eight lines under the chips that already state them. Lengths now say TBA rather than zero, units are singular where they should be, popularity is abbreviated so it fits its cell, an unreleased title says "Starts" instead of "Started", and the duplicates are gone. Rankings, which used to float as loose pills between two cards, are a card with a heading like everything else.

entries.title: Read more appears when there is more to read
entries.detail: The synopsis toggle decided whether to offer itself by counting characters, which was wrong in both directions: at a large font size a 200-character synopsis ran past five lines and the button never appeared, while on a tablet a longer one fitted and the button revealed nothing. It now asks the text whether it was clipped, so the control appears exactly when something is hidden.

entries.title: Controls you can hit, and hear
entries.detail: The action row's buttons were 44dp and are 48; the docked bar's title pill measured about 38dp and is now at least 48. The hero poster was a raw pointer gesture that a screen reader could not reach at all, and it is now a button that announces the title and says what tapping it does. Portraits on the cast, crew and relations rows were describing themselves with the same name printed underneath them, so every card was read out twice; the duplicate descriptions are gone. The play glyph on a theme song is only drawn when there is a video behind it, the chevron that promised a destination over a row that only scrolls sideways is gone, and a studio credit AniList gave no id for is a plain capsule rather than a disabled button.

entries.title: Settings, read top to bottom
entries.detail: The shelf in Settings had a "Network" heading for one row and an "Accounts" heading for another, so the AniList account and the connection check - two questions about the same service - sat in separate sections. They share one section now, under AniList, and every label describes the page behind it. Each card is titled for the setting it holds rather than the page it lives on: "Dashboard" is "Arriving rows", "AniList" on the account page is "AniList Client ID" with a line saying the default works. The About page reads build, updates, what's new, diagnostics, privacy, links in that order, and the quick-add hold picker is the same segmented control the Theme page uses instead of a tab bar padded for the edge of a screen.

entries.title: The palette and hue pickers say what they are
entries.detail: In Appearance, the palette cards never told a screen reader which one was selected, and the check mark carried the palette's own name as a description on top of the name drawn under the swatch - so the selected card was read out twice and the other three said nothing about being the alternative. Both report their state now. The custom hue dots are a colour and no text at all, so they were anonymous until picked; they name themselves now, and the row says that tapping the selected hue again goes back to the palette. The Motion description was rewritten while I was in there: Instant, Smooth and Chill are three sentences instead of three equals signs.

entries.title: Reset appears when there is something to reset
entries.detail: The Appearance page offers "Reset appearance" when anything on it differs from the default, and it was not counting the anime retain/revert pair - both of which the reset clears. A reader who had turned retention off, or moved the revert timer to ten minutes, had something to reset and no button offering it. On the Library page the refresh card's reset says "Reset to 30 min" now instead of "Use AniSequel's default", which made you go and find out what the default was.

entries.title: Diagnostics reads its report off the main thread
entries.detail: The Diagnostics card in About read the last crash report from disk while it was being drawn. It is one small file and usually absent, so the cost was a frame here and there rather than a hang, but a disk read has no business in composition. The card also stops putting a warning triangle over "Crash reports are off", and its Clear button is "Delete report", which is what it does.

entries.title: Crash reports, and they are off until you say otherwise
entries.detail: The comment sheet has been force-closing while it loads a thread, and the report that comes back is the sentence "it closes when loading the comments" - which is true and unfixable, because a force-stop leaves nothing behind once the system dialog is dismissed and reading the source can only rule a line out. So the next crash can now leave a note: the exception, its stack, the app version and the device model, written to the app's own private storage. It is off by default. Settings > Info > Diagnostics has the switch, the last report when there is one, and Copy / Show / Clear; nothing is ever uploaded, and turning the switch off deletes whatever was stored. If you are reporting a bug, turn it on, reproduce the crash, then come back to that card.

entries.title: The app says where it comes from
entries.detail: AniSequel is installed from GitHub rather than a store, so Settings > Info > Help & links now carries the repository - the download page, the source and the release notes for the build in your hand - with the GitHub mark next to it, and a Report a problem row that opens the issue tracker. That is also where a copied crash report is meant to go.

entries.title: A posted reply scrolls to the right row
entries.detail: Posting a reply scrolls the sheet to it, and the scroll was one row short whenever the refresh above the list had failed: the list's first item is an error row in that case, not a reply, so the target index landed on the comment above the new one and left your own reply just off screen. The offset accounts for the error row now.

entries.title: The empty-state orb breathes instead of tearing
entries.detail: The orb morphs between a nine-lobed cookie and a soft burst now - the adjacent pair from Material's own loading-indicator sequence. The old pair was the nine-sided cookie and an eight-petal flower, and that is not a morph: the two outlines have no stable curve-to-curve correspondence, so the middle of the animation folded through itself and read as a moving version of the torn clover. The icon and the silhouette also share one clock, so the glyph grows through the deformation instead of pulsing on an unrelated 1.6s loop.

entries.title: One icon for an empty list
entries.detail: Profile > Activity and Profile > Library were drawing the same fact - a list with nothing in it - three ways: a comment bubble on Activity, a timer on Library, and a magnifier once the Library's search matched nothing. Both use the list glyph for an ordinary empty list now. The magnifier is kept for a search or a filter that actually narrowed a list, and a filtered Library says "No titles match these filters" instead of claiming the whole list is empty.

entries.title: A calmer, more expressive orb
entries.detail: The morph rests on each silhouette before deforming, then breathes through the change with the icon rather than oscillating without a pause. A soft aura behind the silhouette gives the flat container colour some depth, and the container and glyph colours cross-fade when the empty state changes meaning instead of snapping in one frame. The whole loop is one named motion token, so its rest and travel are tuned together.

entries.title: The tier board expands instead of cutting
entries.detail: Opening a tier list, leaving one, and switching profile tabs share one motion language now: the incoming page travels a short distance, springs up from slightly smaller, and the page underneath recedes rather than sliding away. The switch between the shelf of lists and an open board was a hard cut in the middle of the route - it animates too, keyed on the list's id so a drag or a rename does not replay it. The unranked tray grows up from the bottom edge when a pool appears, the floating buttons ride it instead of jumping a tray's height, and a carried poster springs up as it is picked up. The board's progress bar is drawn by scaling a full-width capsule rather than re-measuring on every frame.

entries.title: Tier exports are sharper, and complete
entries.detail: PNG posters are filled into their rounded tiles with a bitmap shader instead of being clipped and blitted, because Android's path clipping is not anti-aliased - at 4K every cover had a stair-stepped corner sitting inside a smooth outline. The SVG export's translucent colours were written in Android's #AARRGGBB order, which SVG reads as #RRGGBBAA, so white subtitles, captions and the tile hairline all came out mint; they use fill-opacity and stroke-opacity now. The SVG also draws each tier's member count and the poster hairline, clips covers to the same rounded rectangle, and clips a long title or tier name to the page instead of letting it run off. Shared images are pruned from the cache, so sharing a board repeatedly no longer leaves every 4K copy behind.

entries.title: Ani-chan has ninety-two more things to say
entries.detail: The joke pool grew from 475 lines to 567, and every tone gained rather than one. The new material is about the app itself - exporting a board, the widget counting shows while nobody is looking, the heatmap's missing day, the changelog you are reading - and about individual shows: the cut that lands on the drum, the ending theme whose first frame is the finale's last shot, the sequel that exists only in a press release. Three lines were rewritten rather than added because they claimed a placement or a screen the reader might not be on, and two more because they were the weakest in their tone: a joke about the app is only funny while it is true.

entries.title: A preview is no longer cut short
entries.detail: Each trigger now owns the line it put on screen. Before, every effect ended its turn by hiding whatever pill was up, so tapping Preview two seconds into a timed joke had its replacement dismissed the moment the old joke's five seconds expired - and a preview could in turn hide a newer timed line. The worse case was a moment line cancelled by leaving the page: its hide was written after the waiting dwell, so cancellation skipped it and the pill stayed up with nothing left to remove it. A show now carries a token, and only the token that is still current may hide the pill.

entries.title: Readable pills, readable choices
entries.detail: Ani-chan's name and the "Tap to dismiss" caption were drawn at 0.65 and 0.55 alpha over the pill's container, which measured about 4.0:1 and 3.3:1 in the default dark theme - under the 4.5:1 a small label needs, and the unsaved heart was under the 3:1 a control needs. They are raised, and the heart with them. On the Jokes page, the Mixed quick-pick was drawn in the disabled grey while it was the selected state, because the chip tested "disabled" before "selected"; a selected-and-locked chip now reads as selected with only the tap withheld, and a genuinely disabled chip's label is no longer half-transparent.

entries.title: Smaller tier-list fixes
entries.detail: An empty board whose library is still loading no longer offers "No titles left to place" - it says to add titles, which is what its tap actually does. A dragged poster's lift is a real animation now: it was an animation whose target never changed, so the ghost was created already grown and never popped.

entries.title: The empty-state clover moves again
entries.detail: Every empty state in the app - no comments, an empty tier board, a studio with no credits, a filtered library - was drawing the same frozen shape. It was meant to morph between two Material shapes, and the progress was read inside the shape's own outline callback. A clipped layer asks for that outline once, when the layer is set up, so the app captured a single frame of the morph and kept it forever: the lopsided, torn-looking clover. The silhouette is drawn in the draw pass now, so it is rebuilt every frame and actually breathes, and one path and one matrix are reused instead of allocated per frame. The same component covers all ten places the orb appears.

entries.title: A darker tone, and a bigger pool
entries.detail: The joke pool grew from 323 lines to 475. A fifth tone - Dark - holds 70 new lines about cancelled sequels, indefinite hiatuses, adaptations that stop short of the ending and the fictional deaths the hobby is built on, so a reader who wants Ani-chan's voice without the graves can switch that arm off on its own. The other four tones gained 82 lines between them, every tone still has at least 40 of its own, and the shuffle bag cycles the larger filter instead of re-drawing the same handful.

entries.title: Mixed, in one tap
entries.detail: Settings > Jokes > What she talks about now opens with a Mixed preset. It is not a sixth pool: it switches all five tones back on in a single write, so the bag holds the whole pool again without five taps, and it dims the moment one tone is switched off. Because it is one write rather than five, the toast cannot draw from a half-restored filter and a fast tap cannot lose a tone to a race. The card still says how many lines and tones the current mix is drawing from.

entries.title: The activity feed no longer stops early
entries.detail: AniList tells a paged list whether another page exists, and the feed used to ignore that answer and guess from the size of the page it received. The guess is wrong whenever the app drops a row it cannot draw - a list update whose title has since been removed, or a union member that is not a list change - so one filtered row could end a history with hundreds of entries still behind it, with nothing on screen to say why. The feed now pages on AniList's own answer, asks for its page size in one place rather than two, and ends with a quiet "You're all caught up" instead of an unexplained full stop.

entries.title: Refreshing keeps the feed on screen
entries.detail: A refresh over rows that were already loaded replaced all of them with the loading skeleton - and a refresh that failed replaced them with the full-page error. Planning a title from the dashboard while standing on the Activity tab could therefore clear the feed you were reading. A refresh now leaves the rows where they are and swaps in the new page when it lands; a failed one becomes a small Retry row above the feed rather than an error screen, and the profile's refresh button now refreshes an opened Activity tab too, without starting a feed that nobody has looked at.

entries.title: Activity cards are easier to skim
entries.detail: Every status used to be one of two blues, so a dropped title and a finished one looked the same. Completed, watching, planning, rewatching, paused and dropped each have their own tinted pill now, drawn with Material's matching container and on-container colours so the label stays readable under a wallpaper-derived palette. The card also stops downloading the extra-large cover for a 96dp poster - the smaller size is everything the row can show - and the heatmap's legend reads its colours from the same ramp as the grid instead of a copy that could drift from it. Relative times in a feed left open now advance once a minute instead of freezing at the moment the card was drawn.

entries.title: Smaller fixes
entries.detail: Download sizes were formatted with the device's decimal separator, so a phone set to a comma locale showed "2,3 MB" beside an English sentence and read like a thousands separator; they now use a fixed locale. The quick-add button was carrying seven imports it had stopped using, and a set of other screens had accumulated unused imports during earlier passes; those are gone, so a reader chasing a reference no longer lands on a line that does nothing. A finished like on one comment no longer re-enables another comment's heart while its request is still in the air.

entries.title: Covers stay where they were
entries.detail: The cover cache lived in the app's cache directory, which Android may empty whenever it wants the space back - and "Clear cache" in system Settings does the same on request. So the app kept forgetting artwork it had already downloaded: every poster went back to a placeholder and came down the network again, sometimes on a cold start where nothing had changed. Covers now live in private storage that survives a restart, a cache wipe and an update, and the ceiling was raised to 256 MB, enough that a large list no longer reaches the point where old covers are dropped. The cache is keyed on the image address, and AniList changes that address when it changes a cover, so artwork is kept until it is genuinely replaced and the new picture is fetched the first time it is seen. Home-screen widget covers get the same treatment, saved as raw bytes beside the app cache rather than lost with the process.

entries.title: Loading says what it is doing
entries.detail: The Library used to hand its first load to the profile's full-screen spinner, then jump from one dot to twelve posters and a filter bar in a single frame. It now draws the grid that is coming: an expressive header on a tinted surface, with the step's own sentence ("Connecting to AniList to find your list" is not the same as "Loading your AniList profile"), over three columns of shimmering 2:3 tiles. The same header shape is used by the profile's loader, and a cold start that is still reading the stored session now shows the app mark with "Checking for a saved session" instead of a bare dot that was indistinguishable from a screen that had failed.

entries.title: Saved copy stops moving the page
entries.detail: The app paints your saved list before the network answers, which makes a cold start quick - but the notice that said so was a row in the page, so it appeared and disappeared above the first poster and moved everything below it, twice per launch. On Home and the Library it is now part of the top bar's subtitle line, where a second line already exists, so it costs no layout at all; names ellipsize before it rather than pushing it off. On the profile card the chip keeps its own animation but now gives its height back on a spring, so the header settles instead of being yanked, and it wears a quiet surface colour rather than a container that competed with the stats under it.

entries.title: Signing in is one screen, not five
entries.detail: The sign-in card grew a keyboard inset it never had: tapping the username field used to leave it, and the Scan button, behind the keyboard with no way to submit but a key that did nothing. The field now offers Search as its action, hides the keyboard when it submits, and no longer capitalises or auto-corrects a name that has to match exactly. While AniList is being asked, the connect button is replaced in place by a card of exactly its height that says which wait it is - "Waiting for AniList" or "Signed in - opening your list" - so the helper row, the redirect hint and the error card no longer jump during a sign-in, and a reader who has just signed in is not shown the connect button again for a frame. The icon rail also stops advancing while the app is in the browser instead of ticking away behind another app.

entries.title: Ani-chan stays as long as you like
entries.detail: The five-second pill was the one property of the toast you could not change. Beside the pace sits a dwell choice: Quick keeps a line up for 3 seconds, Standard 5, Relaxed 8 and Long 12, and Until tapped leaves it there until you tap it, with a small caption on the pill so that arm does not look stuck. The preview uses the dwell you picked, so the longest lines can be read before you commit to them.

entries.title: You can keep a line you like
entries.detail: Every joke now carries a heart. Tapping it saves the line on the device; Settings has a Saved lines card that lists what you kept in pool order, replays one at the real edge with a tap, and removes or clears them. Saved lines survive Reset joke settings, because they are yours rather than a switch, and a line saved by a build whose pool has since changed is kept rather than silently dropped.

entries.title: Pick what she talks about
entries.detail: The pool is grouped into four tones - Feelings, Backlog, Craft and Ani-chan & the app - and each can be switched off. At least one stays on, and the card tells you how many lines the current filter has. The shuffle bag cycles only the tones you kept, so switching Craft off does not spend eleven draws on lines you will never see. Every tone has at least 42 lines of its own.

entries.title: Ani-chan can be invited, not just scheduled
entries.detail: Besides the timer, three moments can now earn a line: when you open the app, when you change tab, and after you refresh. All three are off by default, and each still waits for a quiet gap after the last line - one greeting per launch, six minutes between tab changes and three after a refresh - so a busy tab is not a drum roll. The sign-in screen stays quiet regardless.

entries.title: A bigger pool, and a quieter arrival
entries.detail: The pool grew to 323 lines, with new material added to every tone rather than one. The arrival tick can now be switched off for a silent pill, the preview respects the dwell and the tone filter instead of only the edge, and the Settings row for Ani-chan is named for what the page now changes.

entries.title: About is about the app again
entries.detail: About & support had become the second account page: it carried the profile card, the sign-in prompt, the list snapshot, a second connection check and a second sign-out button, while the account page was mostly a Client ID field. The profile, the demo note and the list snapshot now live on AniList account, beside the one sign-out button; the connection card is gone because the AniList connection row on the Settings shelf opens the same dialog. About is now five cards with one subject each - the build, privacy, updates, what's new and the documentation link - and the shelf rows take their titles and subtitles from the pages they open, so a row can no longer describe a different page than the one it opens.

entries.title: Comments come back the way you left them
entries.detail: Reopening a thread you had just dismissed used to blank the conversation and redraw the skeleton, and a refresh that failed replaced the comments with an error line. The last thread you read is now kept for the next open: the comments appear at once while a newer copy loads, a failure over them becomes a small banner with its own Retry, and only a thread with nothing to show gets the full-screen explanation. The waiting skeleton now includes the like and reply row, the empty state says what to do instead of looking broken, and the composer opens with the keyboard up, reads Post Comment or Post Reply to match what you are writing, and gives the reply-target's clear button a 40dp target instead of a 28dp one.

entries.title: The tier list can be searched by name
entries.detail: The filter sheet has a search field above the status chips. It matches the name on the poster and AniList's English, romaji and native names, so shingeki finds Attack on Titan; every word you type has to match, in any order, so attack titan and titan attack both work. The field shows how many titles matched and has a clear button, searches apply to the board, the unranked shelf and the exported image, and clearing the search leaves the status, genre and studio filters exactly as they were. Nothing is removed from your list, and the filter dot on the app bar lights for a search the same way it does for any other filter.

entries.title: Names can sit where you want, and be as long as you want
entries.detail: Display options already let a name sit under the cover or on it; beside that choice is now a length - Short, Standard or Full. Short keeps a dense board readable at a glance, Full prints the whole title, and the default cuts a name at a sensible point with an ellipsis. The board, the PNG export and the SVG export all read the same setting, so a file cannot show more of a name than the screen it came from.

entries.title: The exports now match the board
entries.detail: Three divergences closed. The SVG writer used to draw a caption under every poster no matter what the board showed, including when names were turned off or moved onto the artwork; it now reads the same title settings and draws the on-cover scrim. The PNG put the score badge in the top corner even when the name was across the top, where the two overlapped - it moves to the bottom like the board's. And both exporters now centre a caption from the font's own metrics instead of a constant baseline, so a descender is no longer clipped at the bottom of the image.

entries.title: Ani-chan remembers which joke she told
entries.detail: The random toast now draws from a shuffle bag: every line appears once before any line is repeated, so a joke you read an hour ago cannot come back while there are still new ones. The pool grew by eighteen lines, the first joke arrives sooner - 45 seconds to two minutes rather than one and a half to four - and the pill has an Ani-chan label, a tinted sparkle and a hairline edge so it reads as the app speaking rather than as a notification from nobody.

entries.title: Faster filters, and a faster vector export
entries.detail: The name filter builds one lowercased haystack per title when the library loads, instead of lowercasing every title on every keystroke, and normalises the query once per filter value rather than once per candidate. The SVG writer looks each tile's title up in one map instead of scanning the whole candidate list per poster, which turns a 300-title export from 90,000 comparisons into 300. A failed PNG render now recycles the bitmap it had already allocated, instead of leaving the largest allocation in the app to the collector.

entries.title: Smaller board fixes
entries.detail: The filter dot counts a name search as a filter; Show everything and Default both clear the search; a pasted paragraph is capped at 64 characters rather than becoming an unbounded query; and the keyboard's Search key puts the keyboard away instead of running a second, different filter. The export sheet's description now says the name search is included.

entries.title: Settings is a shelf now, not three tabs
entries.detail: Info, Theme and Edit named the files the screen was built from, not the things you wanted to change, and Edit carried refresh, arrival rows, quick add, the Client ID, the app lock and sign-out because they had nowhere else to go. Settings now opens on a shelf of rounded icon rows - Appearance, Jokes, Library & dashboard, AniList account, AniList connection and About & support - and each row opens a focused page. The old Edit tab was split in two, so refresh and quick add live together and the account page holds the session and the lock. Every old control is still there under a name that says what it does, and the screen closes with the round button in the corner.

entries.title: Ani-chan can be tuned, moved, and previewed
entries.detail: The joke pool more than doubled to 178 lines, and the shuffle bag still shows every line once before repeating any. Settings now lets you choose the pace - Calm, Normal or Chatty - and whether the pill sits at the top or the bottom edge. You can also choose whether jokes stay on the main pages or are allowed over pages you open from them, such as Settings, the tier list and a title; the sign-in screen stays quiet either way. Turning jokes off keeps the pace you chose, so turning them back on does not silently reset it, and a Preview button asks the real toast to appear at the edge you picked, even while jokes are off. The card still lives in Settings and is saved on the device.

entries.title: The connection check is straight with you
entries.detail: The Settings-side AniList check used to borrow the random failure quips, so a diagnostic you asked for could answer with a joke about naps. It no longer pulls from the joke pool: every line in that dialog now says what actually happened, and a probe that cannot finish says so plainly instead of rerolling. The heart, the status strip and the go-touch-grass exit are unchanged, and the ambient Ani-chan toast is the only place random lines appear.

entries.title: The lock is a real view-only mode
entries.detail: Locking the board now stops every edit, not just the long-press drag: a tap no longer opens the placement sheet, and the unranked shelf will not start a drag or open the picker. The shelf dims and its header says View only instead of offering Browse all, a pill at the top of the board says the same and unlocks in one tap, and Add is disabled until the lock comes off. Scrolling and pinching keep working the whole time, because those are how a locked board is read.

entries.title: One finger scrolls the board again
